newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-AUSTRIAN'S FACE TOUGH QUALIFICATION BATTLE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-AUSTRIAN'S FACE TOUGH QUALIFICATION BATTLE.

text.p: Austrian alpine skiers will once again feel the pressures of racing for an elite team at the two World Cup downhills and one slalom race in Kitzbuehel from Friday to Sunday.

With a little under two weeks to go before the start of the world championships in Sestriere, most of the nation's top class downhill and slalom skiers are still fighting for a starting bib at the Italian resort.
The two-run sprint downhill and the full-length traditional "Hahnenkamm" race on the dreaded Streif piste in Kitzbuehel, will mark the last chance Austrian downhillers have to qualify.
So far, only Patrick Ortlieb has a fixed place in the downhill team for Sestriere, as he is the defending world champion in the discipline.

The other four Austrian starting places have to be fought out between Fritz Strobl, Werner Franz, Joseph Strobl, Hans Knauss and Guenther Mader -- while Andreas Schifferer, Hannes Trinkl and Roland Assinger also still have slim chances.
From these eight, only Fritz Strobl is in the lucky position of having won a downhill this season when he clinched his maiden World Cup victory in Val D'Isere in December.
Strobl is also the only skier other than Italy's Kristian Ghedina and Frenchman Luc Alphand to have won a downhill this winter.
However, neither current downhill standings leader Ghedina nor defending title-holder Alphand, are prepared to take unnecessary risks in Kitzbuehel.
Ghedina, who won this season in Val Gardena, Chamonix and Wengen, is momentarily suffering from back troubles and has difficulties getting into the downhill tuck position.
"I want to be fit for Sestriere, that is the most important thing for me," said Ghedina. "It is not often that a skier gets the chance to win a world championship medal in front of a home crowd."
Alphand, who took races in Val Gardena and Bormio in December, is still in shock after his compatriot and roommate Adrien Duvillards crashed heavily during a training run in Wengen last week.

"Of course I would like another victory in Kitzbuehel, but I will be playing it safe. My goal is a medal in Sestriere," said Alphand, winner of both Kitzbuehel downhills which were staged on the same day in 1995.
Austrian slalom skiers also have two races to go -- in Kitzbuehel on Sunday and near-by Schladming on Janua
